title: Fresh branch clients cannot obtain a lease
scenario: R1 connects clients on Gi0/0, 10.10.10.1/24, to R2 through Gi0/1, 10.10.20.1/24. R2 is the server at 10.10.20.2/24. DHCP service is enabled on both routers. A new PC has no prior lease; an older PC still has a valid lease and can reach a server. Links and VLAN membership are verified. The following abbreviated records are representative teaching evidence.

exhibits.title: R1 relevant interface configuration
exhibits.text:
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 ip address 10.10.10.1 255.255.255.0
!
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 ip address 10.10.20.1 255.255.255.0
 ip helper-address 10.10.20.2

exhibits.title: R2 pool and return-path checks
exhibits.text:
Pool USERS network: 10.10.10.0/24
Ordinary host addresses: 254
Excluded: 10.10.10.1–10.10.10.49 (49)
Active bindings: 2
Conflicts: none
Route: 10.10.10.0/24 via 10.10.20.1
Ping to 10.10.10.1: successful

exhibits.title: Current attempt capture
exhibits.text:
Client-side capture: DHCPDISCOVER arrives at R1 Gi0/0.
Server-side capture: no matching forwarded Discover reaches R2.

question: Which demonstrated configuration mistake should be corrected first?
options: The matching DHCP pool is exhausted by its active bindings.
The server lacks a return route toward the client subnet.
The helper is configured on the server-facing interface.
The server has no pool matching the relayed client subnet.
explanation: The client broadcast arrives on Gi0/0, but only Gi0/1 has the helper. Move it to the receiving client interface. Capacity is not exhausted: 254 − 49 − 2 = 203 addresses are available under the stated conditions. The return route is supplied. An old client can keep working with a valid lease; its later unicast renewal might also work without this helper, so it does not validate initial relay acquisition.
fix:
Move the helper, then repeat the fresh client request.

```ios
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/1
R1(config-if)# no ip helper-address 10.10.20.2
R1(config-if)# interface gigabitethernet0/0
R1(config-if)# ip helper-address 10.10.20.2
R1(config-if)# end
R1# show ip interface gigabitethernet0/0
```

Verify a new R2 binding and the client’s actual address, mask, gateway, and DNS setting. Test the gateway and intended remote service. Save the corrected configuration after verification.

title: The fourth training-room client receives no lease
scenario: An isolated training room uses R1 as a verified relay and R2 as an IOS DHCP server. The first three clients still have valid leases and are powered on. A fourth fresh client receives no allocation. Its Discover reaches R2. The reserved infrastructure range is .1–.49; the upper exclusion was temporary for this exercise. These are representative records, not simulator captures.

exhibits.title: R2 pool configuration
exhibits.text:
ip dhcp excluded-address 10.10.10.1 10.10.10.49
ip dhcp excluded-address 10.10.10.53 10.10.10.254
ip dhcp pool USERS
 network 10.10.10.0 255.255.255.0
 default-router 10.10.10.1
 dns-server 10.10.20.53
 lease 0 8 0

exhibits.title: Current allocation and conflict checks
exhibits.text:
Active leases: 10.10.10.50, 10.10.10.51, 10.10.10.52
Conflict entries: none
Fourth client's Discover received; no new binding recorded.

question: Which repair restores capacity while preserving the intended static-address range and healthy leases?
options: Clear all three active bindings and retry the fourth client.
Remove the temporary .53–.254 exclusion and retry the fourth client.
Reconfigure the verified helper to point to the local gateway.
Remove only the .1–.49 exclusion and retry the fourth client.
explanation: The two exclusions leave only .50–.52, all of which are occupied. Removing the temporary upper exclusion expands the candidate range to .50–.254, 205 addresses, while preserving static infrastructure. Broadly deleting bindings risks allocating an address still in use. Changing a working helper does not add capacity; removing gateway protection is unsafe. Existing eight-hour leases can expire or be released; they are not permanent.
fix:
Remove only the temporary exclusion.

```ios
R2# configure terminal
R2(config)# no ip dhcp excluded-address 10.10.10.53 10.10.10.254
R2(config)# end
R2# show ip dhcp pool
R2# show ip dhcp binding
```

Retry DHCP on the fourth client, confirm its new address is outside .1–.49 and distinct from active clients, and test the gateway. Verify all original clients retain service. Save after the check.
